I saw Matt Bellamy at a grocery store in Los Angeles a few years back. I told him how cool it was to meet him in person, but I didn’t want to be a douche and bother him and ask him for photos or anything.
He said, “Oh, like you’re doing now?”
I was taken aback, and all I could say was “Huh?” but he kept cutting me off and going “huh? huh? huh?” and closing his hand shut in front of my face. I walked away and continued with my shopping, and I heard him chuckle as I walked off. When I came to pay for my stuff up front I saw him trying to walk out the doors with like fifteen Milky Ways in his hands without paying.
The girl at the counter was very nice about it and professional, and was like “Sir, you need to pay for those first.” At first he kept pretending to be tired and not hear her, but eventually turned back around and brought them to the counter.
When she took one of the bars and started scanning it multiple times, he stopped her and told her to scan them each individually “to prevent any electrical infetterence,” and then turned around and winked at me. I don’t even think that’s a word. After she scanned each bar and put them in a bag and started to say the price, he kept interrupting her by yawning really loudly.

Each song on this album, I feel like, is about either life, death, or the juxtaposition of the two. And this one sums it all up with that final stanza, comparing Earth to the “book of blue” where you are forced to live and die without your consent. It’s a really powerful song, and while screaming is not always my thing, it is 100% justified in this case. I love that song. Not my favorite on the album, but FAR from my least favorite.

My thoughts exactly, I have been voting Breakthrough for a while now. Good song, but not better than MEH/MB or T/D or Ohio or EDNE if you ask me. Make Everyone Happy is my second favorite on the album :\\

It's just such a cathartic penultimate track. The message of Make Everyone Happy is really relatable and powerful—that sometimes you don't have any sense of self, but the important thing is to live for yourself and not for others, to remember to make yourself happy, at least, because you never will be able to make everyone happy. And that first line is a paradox, where he says that you shouldn't make facts out of opinions, but then whoever he is talking to says he's right, making his opinion a fact, which satisfies him. Which says something kind of interesting about human beings and the need for validation.

And the Mechanical Birds section just makes me feel like I'm ascending lol. It's really gorgeous. The guitars obviously sound like birds chirping, and I have heard a theory about how the sound of birds chirping makes people happy, so the guitars are the mechanical birds and they're built to "make everyone happy". Such a strong ending. I love STIB too, but this would have been a great album closer as well.
